title: Occupant load and egress
prompt:
A single-story tenant fit-out has these spaces. The area given for each is the one its load factor applies to (net or gross, as marked).

| Space | Area | Occupant load factor |
|---|---|---|
| Mercantile — sales floor | 5,930 sq ft (gross) | 60 sq ft per occupant |
| Business areas | 5,770 sq ft (gross) | 150 sq ft per occupant |
| Exercise room | 3,920 sq ft (gross) | 50 sq ft per occupant |

Rules for this jurisdiction: occupant load of each space = its area ÷ its load factor, rounded UP per space; the floor's occupant load is the sum. Exits required: 1 for up to 49 occupants, 2 for 50–500, 3 for 501–1,000, 4 above 1,000. Minimum total egress width at doors is 0.2 inch per occupant.
Give the total occupant load, the number of exits required, and the minimum total egress width in inches.
Answer keys: "total_occupant_load" (integer), "required_exits" (integer), "min_egress_width_in" (number).

Answer keys: "risers" (integer), "riser_height_in" (number), "treads" (integer), "total_run_in" (number).

Give the proposed gross floor area, the maximum floor area the FAR allows, whether it complies ("yes"/"no"), and the margin in sq ft (allowed − proposed; negative if over).

title: Asphalt paving tonnage
prompt:
Pave 10,000 square yards with a 2.0 in base course and a 1.5 in surface course of hot-mix asphalt. Use 112 lb per square yard per inch of compacted thickness and add 3% waste to the total. Give tons of base, tons of surface (before waste), and total tons including waste (2,000 lb per ton).
Answer keys: "base_course_tons" (number), "surface_course_tons" (number), "total_tons_with_waste" (number).

title: Differential leveling loop
prompt:
A level loop starts and ends on BM-1 (elevation 385.591 ft) and sets finished-floor control point FF-A. Each line is one instrument setup: a backsight (BS) on the first point and a foresight (FS) on the next.

| From | BS (ft) | To | FS (ft) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM-1 | 8.486 | TP1 | 5.366 |
| TP1 | 4.501 | TP2 | 6.595 |
| TP2 | 4.655 | TP3 | 6.278 |
| TP3 | 8.760 | FF-A | 7.686 |
| FF-A | 9.081 | TP9 | 6.610 |
| TP9 | 8.488 | TP10 | 10.837 |
| TP10 | 5.362 | BM-1 | 6.009 |

Height of instrument = elevation + BS; next elevation = height of instrument − FS. Carry unadjusted elevations around the loop (no adjustment). Give FF-A's elevation, the misclosure (computed closing elevation of BM-1 − its known elevation), the allowable misclosure = 0.05 × √(loop length in miles) with the loop 5,775 ft long, and whether |misclosure| is within it ("yes"/"no").
Answer keys: "ff_a_elevation_ft" (number), "misclosure_ft" (number), "allowable_ft" (number), "within_tolerance" (string).

title: Embodied carbon of a take-off
prompt:
Embodied carbon (A1–A3) for a 23,216 m² building, from its material take-off and the project's chosen emission factors:

| Material | Quantity | Factor |
|---|---|---|
| Structural steel sections | 72.8 t | 1,550 kgCO₂e per t |
| Mineral wool insulation | 2,545.9 m³ | 45 kgCO₂e per m³ |
| Aluminium curtain wall framing | 271.6 t | 9,200 kgCO₂e per t |
| Float glass | 508.8 t | 1,400 kgCO₂e per t |

Give the total in tonnes CO₂e, the intensity in kgCO₂e per m² of floor area, the material contributing most, and the saving in tonnes if the factor for "Aluminium curtain wall framing" is reduced by 30% (quantity unchanged).
Answer keys: "total_tCO2e" (number), "kgCO2e_per_m2" (number), "largest_contributor" (string), "saving_tCO2e" (number).

title: Energy use intensity and cost
prompt:
A 382,448 sq ft office used 8,321,100 kWh of electricity and 48,440 therms of natural gas last year. Electricity costs $0.205/kWh and gas $0.93/therm. Using 3.412 kBtu per kWh and 100 kBtu per therm, give the site energy use intensity (kBtu per sq ft per year), the annual energy cost, and cost per sq ft.
Answer keys: "site_eui_kbtu_per_sf" (number), "annual_energy_cost" (number), "cost_per_sf" (number).

title: Rooftop solar sizing and payback
prompt:
A 41,046 sq ft roof has 65% of its area usable for PV. Modules are 430 W, 22.3 sq ft each (whole modules only, round down). The site produces 1,450 kWh per kW-DC per year. Installed cost is $2.53/W-DC before a 0% incentive, and the building pays $0.248/kWh. Give the number of modules, system size in kW-DC, annual kWh, and simple payback in years (net cost ÷ annual savings).
Answer keys: "panels" (integer), "system_kw_dc" (number), "annual_kwh" (number), "simple_payback_years" (number).

title: Development pro forma
prompt:
A 94-unit apartment development: land $13,200,000, hard costs $215,000 per unit, soft costs 28% of hard costs. Stabilized rent averages $3,500 per unit per month, vacancy and credit loss 7% of gross potential rent, operating expenses 38% of effective gross income. Exit cap rate 4.75%.
Give total development cost, net operating income (NOI), yield on cost (NOI ÷ total cost, as a percent), stabilized value (NOI ÷ cap rate), and profit margin ((value − cost) ÷ cost, as a percent).
Answer keys: "total_development_cost" (number), "noi" (number), "yield_on_cost_pct" (number), "stabilized_value" (number), "profit_margin_pct" (number).

title: Lifecycle cost (NPV) of two options
prompt:
Compare two options for a rooftop units over 20 years at a 5% real discount rate. Option A: $340,000 installed, $64,000 per year to run and maintain. Option B: $538,000 installed, $44,000 per year. Annual costs are paid at the end of each year; no salvage value. Give the present value of each option's total cost and which has the lower lifecycle cost ("A" or "B").
Answer keys: "present_value_cost_a" (number), "present_value_cost_b" (number), "lower_lifecycle_cost" (string).

title: Maintenance backlog priority
prompt:
Prioritize this facilities maintenance backlog. Condition is 1 (failed) to 5 (like new); criticality is 1 (low) to 5 (life safety). Risk score = (6 − condition) × criticality, plus 5 if the asset has reached or passed its expected life (age ≥ life). Ties break alphabetically.

| Asset | Condition | Criticality | Age (yr) | Expected life (yr) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boiler B-1 | 1 | 4 | 13 | 30 |
| Generator G-1 | 3 | 4 | 20 | 25 |
| Elevator 2 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 15 |
| Switchgear MDP | 2 | 4 | 9 | 25 |
| Domestic water heater | 4 | 3 | 4 | 30 |
| Parking deck joints | 4 | 4 | 11 | 30 |
| Cooling tower CT-1 | 5 | 3 | 19 | 25 |
| AHU-1 | 4 | 5 | 12 | 15 |
| Roof section C | 4 | 2 | 21 | 25 |

Give the top-priority asset, the top three in order as one comma-separated string, and the top score.
Answer keys: "top_priority" (string), "top_three" (array (in order)), "top_score" (integer).

title: Concrete strength acceptance
prompt:
Concrete for a slab on J-1733 is specified at f'c = 6,000 psi. Each strength test is the average of the two 28-day cylinders broken from one sample, in placement order:

| Test | Cylinder A (psi) | Cylinder B (psi) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7,250 | 7,000 |
| 2 | 5,800 | 6,230 |
| 3 | 6,700 | 6,730 |
| 4 | 5,950 | 5,870 |
| 5 | 6,190 | 6,170 |
| 6 | 6,290 | 6,390 |
| 7 | 6,890 | 7,070 |
| 8 | 6,300 | 6,270 |
| 9 | 6,840 | 7,170 |

Acceptance rule: (1) every average of three consecutive strength tests must be at least f'c; and (2) no single strength test may fall more than 500 psi below f'c when f'c is 5,000 psi or less, or below 0.90 × f'c when f'c is more than 5,000 psi. Give the lowest strength test, the lowest three-consecutive-test average, how many three-test averages are below f'c, how many single tests are below the individual limit, and whether the concrete is "acceptable" or "not acceptable" (both rules must hold).
Answer keys: "lowest_test_psi" (number), "lowest_three_test_average_psi" (number), "failing_three_test_averages" (integer), "tests_below_individual_limit" (integer), "acceptable" (string).

title: Field compaction tests
prompt:
Structural fill under a footing is specified at 98% relative compaction (field dry density ÷ laboratory maximum dry density) with moisture within ±2 percentage points of optimum. The modified Proctor gives a maximum dry density of 121.6 pcf at 12.6% optimum moisture. Field tests:

| Test | Wet density (pcf) | Moisture (%) |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | 133.8 | 9.8 |
| T2 | 134.4 | 11.0 |
| T3 | 127.0 | 10.3 |
| T4 | 131.4 | 13.9 |
| T5 | 135.3 | 13.6 |
| T6 | 141.7 | 14.3 |

Dry density = wet density ÷ (1 + moisture/100). A test passes only if both the compaction and the moisture requirement are met (boundaries pass). Give the failing test ids in test order, the percent of tests passing, and the average relative compaction of all tests (percent).
Answer keys: "failing_tests" (array (in order)), "percent_passing" (number), "average_relative_compaction_pct" (number).

title: Delay claim and liquidated damages
prompt:
A $6,481,000 lump-sum contract started 2025-05-19 with substantial completion due 2026-04-11. Liquidated damages are $2,500 per calendar day, capped at 5% of the contract sum. Extended general conditions are $3,650 per day. Delay events (all on the critical path, calendar days):

| Event | Cause | Days | Of which concurrent with contractor delay |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | owner (late design change / access) | 20 | 0 |
| 2 | owner (late design change / access) | 34 | 17 |
| 3 | contractor (late submittals) | 26 | — |
| 4 | owner (late design change / access) | 23 | 11 |
| 5 | owner (late design change / access) | 16 | 4 |

Contract rules: owner delays and unusually severe weather are excusable (the completion date extends by their full days); only owner delays are compensable, and owner-delay days that were concurrent with a contractor delay are excusable but not compensable; contractor delays earn nothing. Substantial completion was actually achieved on 2026-07-20. Give the time extension, the compensable days, the days late against the extended date (0 if on time), the liquidated damages (after the cap), the contractor's delay damages (compensable days × extended general conditions), and the net to the contractor (delay damages − liquidated damages).
Answer keys: "extension_days" (integer), "compensable_days" (integer), "days_late" (integer), "liquidated_damages" (number), "delay_damages" (number), "net_to_contractor" (number).

title: Notice, lien and prompt-payment deadlines
prompt:
Summit Drywall & Acoustics first furnished labor on 2026-09-19 and last furnished on 2026-11-01. The statute (as stated here) requires: a preliminary notice within 20 days after first furnishing; a lien recorded within 90 days after last furnishing; and a suit to foreclose within 365 days after the lien is recorded. Every period is calendar days counted from the day after the event, and a deadline that falls on a Saturday or Sunday moves to the following Monday (ignore holidays). The lien was recorded on 2027-01-27.
Separately, its $49,575.57 invoice was received on 2026-10-07; payment is due 45 days after receipt (no weekend adjustment) and was made on 2026-12-30. Late payment bears simple interest of 2.0% per 30 days, prorated by day.
Give the three statutory deadlines, the payment due date, the days paid late, and the interest due.
Answer keys: "preliminary_notice_deadline" (string YYYY-MM-DD), "lien_recording_deadline" (string YYYY-MM-DD), "foreclosure_deadline" (string YYYY-MM-DD), "payment_due_date" (string YYYY-MM-DD), "days_paid_late" (integer), "interest_due" (number).

title: Clash detection on bounding boxes
prompt:
Coordinate the ceiling zone of one structural bay on Alder House Condominiums (J-1290). The federated model's elements are exported as axis-aligned bounding boxes in millimetres (project coordinates):

| ID | Discipline | Element | X min | X max | Y min | Y max | Z min | Z max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-01 | STR | Steel beam W18 | 0 | 12000 | 5650 | 5880 | 3125 | 3575 |
| S-02 | STR | Steel beam W21 | 0 | 12000 | 3400 | 3610 | 3225 | 3755 |
| S-03 | STR | Concrete column | 9700 | 10100 | 1000 | 1400 | 0 | 4200 |
| M-01 | MECH | Supply duct 600×500 | 4400 | 5000 | 0 | 10000 | 2600 | 3100 |
| M-02 | MECH | Supply duct 1200×500 | 8050 | 9250 | 0 | 10000 | 3000 | 3500 |
| P-01 | PLMB | Drain pipe Ø160 | 0 | 12000 | 2175 | 2335 | 3025 | 3185 |
| P-02 | PLMB | Drain pipe Ø110 | 0 | 12000 | 7500 | 7610 | 3250 | 3360 |
| E-01 | ELEC | Cable tray 300×100 | 0 | 12000 | 3400 | 3700 | 2875 | 2975 |

Clash rules: only pairs from different disciplines are tested. A hard clash is a pair whose boxes overlap by more than 0 mm on all three axes (touching faces are not a hard clash). For every other pair, the clearance distance is √(gx² + gy² + gz²), where on each axis the gap is max(0, B min − A max, A min − B max); a pair with no hard clash and a clearance distance under 100 mm is a clearance clash. Give the hard-clash pairs (each written as the two IDs in alphabetical order joined by "/", e.g. "M-01/S-02"), the number of clearance clashes, the hard-clash pair with the largest overlap volume, and that volume in cubic metres.
Answer keys: "hard_clash_pairs" (array), "clearance_clash_count" (integer), "largest_overlap_pair" (string), "largest_overlap_volume_m3" (number).

title: 5D cost from a model schedule
prompt:
Price this model element schedule for Mason Street Retail (J-1255), a renovation and addition. Quantities are the model's, by Uniformat II element code:

| Element | Uniformat | Description | Phase | Quantity | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EL-1375 | C3020 | Floor finishes | New | 3,169 | SF |
| EL-2587 | D3040 | HVAC distribution | New | 2,619 | LF |
| EL-3735 | B2010 | Exterior walls | New | 3,825 | SF |
| EL-4881 | A1030 | Slab on grade | New | 1,829 | SF |
| EL-5783 | B1010 | Floor construction | New | 4,832 | SF |
| EL-6242 | B1010 | Floor construction | New | 6,953 | SF |
| EL-7604 | D3040 | HVAC distribution | Existing | 7,019 | LF |
| EL-8337 | B2010 | Exterior walls | New | 3,388 | SF |
| EL-9723 | A1030 | Slab on grade | New | 2,321 | SF |

Unit rates:

| Uniformat | Rate |
|---|---|

| A1030 | $10.58 per SF |
| B1010 | $29.87 per SF |
| B2010 | $62.59 per SF |
